# Fractional AI Governance Advisor

**Proposal for Tamarack Instruments**
Prepared for Dana Whitfield, General Counsel

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands, operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States, and has about 1,100 staff. Its AI maturity is at the piloting stage:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. The Client is targeting ISO/IEC 42001, with work to start next year. The start date is not fixed and is rendered `Unknown`.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded no inventory of AI systems. The Client's incumbent frameworks are an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function.

The engagement must respect three stated constraints:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

The stated objective, in Dana Whitfield's words, is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

The Client has not completed a prior Academy program, so there are no carried-forward open items.

## 2. The Case for Continuous Fractional Advisory

At the piloting stage, governance decisions arrive in sequence rather than all at once. Over the coming year these include:

- a pilot moving toward production;
- a deployed system that needs review against the data residency constraint;
- a planned system that needs authorization before it is built;
- a certification effort whose start date is still open.

A one-time assessment would capture one moment of this sequence. A fractional advisor stays with the Client as each decision comes due. Each decision is tested against the three principles of the program.

- **Slow AI** holds that AI that cannot be governed, explained and audited is not deployed; the three tests are conjunctive, and the doctrine is a precondition, not a speed limit.
- **Informed Intent** holds that no AI system acts without prior authorization stating its purpose, authority, boundaries and exit, given by a human who meets the five authorizer conditions.
- **Final Liability rests with the Human** holds that every material outcome attaches to a named human owner with decision rights, oversight and the power to intervene.

The program draws on three references:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)
- AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards), used for executive and board-layer reporting

## 3. The Annual Arc

The engagement start date is `Unknown`. The arc front-loads visual inspection governance so that it precedes the stated Q2 2027 production milestone. If the start date compresses that window, the Quarter 1 scope will be reprioritized at intake.

ISO/IEC 42001 audit preparation intensity rises in Quarters 3 and 4. It will be resequenced once the Client fixes a start date.

**Quarter 1: Stabilize.**
- Respond to the June 2026 internal audit finding by building an AI system inventory using GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) templates.
- Prepare an Informed Intent authorization for visual inspection stating purpose, authority, boundaries and exit, with a named owner.
- Review the customer service chatbot against the EU data residency constraint.
- Flag EU AI Act classification questions for each system for external counsel verification.
- Prepare inputs the Client may use in any works council consultation.

**Quarter 2: Deepen.**
- Support a production readiness decision for visual inspection, tested against the three Slow AI conditions using Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen).
- Define oversight and intervention arrangements for the named owner.
- Establish or mature an AI risk register.
- Scope an ISO/IEC 42001 gap assessment.

**Quarter 3: Assure.**
- Conduct the ISO/IEC 42001 gap assessment and design evidence collection.
- Map where AI management system requirements could align with existing management system structures, subject to intake confirmation of what those structures contain.
- Hold a readiness review with the internal audit function.

**Quarter 4: Evolve.**
- Take AI sales forecasting through Informed Intent authorization before build.
- Assess ISO/IEC 42001 readiness.
- Prepare executive and board-layer reporting.
- Prepare a Month 11 renewal and handover options memo.

All audit preparation is expressed as readiness. The program does not promise certification or audit outcomes.

## 4. Cadence and Access Model

- **Executive advisory session:** monthly.
- **Working session with the governance team:** monthly.
- **Asynchronous availability:** for defined question categories, with response windows and escalation paths to be agreed at intake.
- **Quarterly governance review:** against the annual arc.

The roles identified for this engagement are General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors. Attendance for each session is `Unknown` and will be confirmed at intake.

## 5. Scope

**In scope:**
- governance evolution
- implementation guidance
- audit preparation
- AI strategy
- executive decision support

**Out of scope:**
- legal advice
- certification body functions
- staff augmentation
- incident command

The advisor is not counsel of record. Legal questions, including EU AI Act and GDPR interpretation, route to external counsel. Regulatory developments raised in the program are flagged for verification and are not presented as settled advice.

## 6. Investment

The fee is US$10,000 per month for a 12-month term, renewable. Two budget points will be confirmed at intake:

- the fiscal year boundaries;
- how the monthly fee aligns with the budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
